title: Artemis C: arm B data plus gated, human-reviewed teacher labels, QLoRA SFT
status_detail: Prepared on 2026-10-19 in Mission 001. Blocked three ways: benchmark v0 has no train split, the teacher policy has no counsel sign-off (legal_signoff pending), and no teacher was served. No teacher output exists.
hypothesis: At equal training tokens and steps, adding teacher labels from self-hosted gpt-oss-120b and Gemma 4 31B-it that passed the deterministic checks, the teacher gate and human review improves over arm B on adversarial_holdout (classes I subcode confusion and K real-world dates) and on non-ko/en questions, because the student sees more phrasings of the same verified labels (training-distill.md §4.1 H2).
null_hypothesis: Arm C is not better than arm B beyond the CI, or it adds critical errors inherited from the teachers. Then distillation is not worth its review and licence cost, and arm B (or the rules) stands.

baselines.what: Same student, same hyper-parameters, human-reviewed gold only.
baselines.known_limits: Must have passed G1 itself; otherwise arm C is not run.

baselines.what: Best deterministic classifier after cheap rule fixes.

base_model.license_note: Apache-2.0 per HF cardData; keep licence text and NOTICE with any distributed adapter. A student trained on Gemma 4 or gpt-oss outputs carries no extra naming duty under Apache-2.0 (models.md §4), but every teacher condition in configs/teacher_policy.json must be acknowledged on each record.
base_model.loader_note: Same UNVERIFIED loader question as arm B (models.md §8).

secondary_model.note: Only after E4B passes G1 in arm C.

teachers.hardware: one 80 GB GPU with native MXFP4 (training-distill.md §3.1 row 8, LIVE L31)
one 40-80 GB GPU (training-distill.md §3.3; models.md §3b about 20 GB at 4-bit, INFERRED)

train.note: EMPTY: there is no train split and no teacher ledger. Build order: (1) arm B's reviewed gold; (2) teachers label the train prompts only, never dev/test/adversarial_holdout prompts (training-distill.md §4.6); (3) each answer becomes a TeacherRecord with structured labels only; (4) deterministic checks, the teacher gate and human review; (5) survivors become teacher_generated examples whose expected equals the gated output; (6) mix with the gold about 1:1 and subsample to arm B's tokens and steps (training-distill.md §4.2). Every train question needs both Artemis labels (classification and entity extraction) because the runner asks one prompt for both tasks.

leakage_guard.why: Same guard as arm B; teacher paraphrases of eval questions are the main new leakage risk, so the threshold is not relaxed for this arm.

label_rules: One SFT record per question. The runner asks one prompt and one 7-key schema for both Artemis tasks, so a train question needs both its status_procedure_classification and its entity_date_extraction example (same exact question text and payload code); a question with only one label is refused, never completed with a guess.

The classification label must state current_status and target_status (null allowed) and needs_clarification (true or false) explicitly; dates come from the entity label. not_status_tokens and status_codes are scoring labels, not target keys.
The target is that 7-key object as compact JSON in the runner's schema key order; no reasoning text, no evidence text, no legal content.
A teacher label is a candidate, never gold: it needs passing deterministic checks, a teacher gate pass and human review (machine_checked at least; human_verified for critical examples).
A teacher is never asked for reasoning; records keep the final JSON only and the gate refuses reasoning keys or <think> markers.

prompt.defined_in: waymaker_ai/evaluation/baselines/model.py (build_messages, system_prompt, DECODING) and waymaker_ai/evaluation/predictions.py (model_output_schema); sft_dataset.prompt_sha256 hashes all three
prompt.note: Training and evaluation use the runner's own openai_compatible request: one system prompt and one 7-key schema for both Artemis tasks, user message = question (prefixed by the UI payload code when present). A change to the runner's prompt, schema or decoding changes this hash and the config stops loading.

distillation.kind: response-level (sequence) distillation of structured labels, filtered; no logit distillation
distillation.why: Teacher and student vocabularies differ (gpt-oss vs Gemma) and API-style serving returns no full distributions (training-distill.md §2.1 logit-KD row with verifier correction). Label-only targets keep the student from imitating a teacher's prose.

teacher_decoding.reasoning: never requested; use the lowest reasoning setting the serving stack exposes and keep only the final channel

distillation.gate: waymaker_ai.distillation.teacher_policy.gate_record (policy recomputed at build time; legal_signoff must be approved)
distillation.human_review: at least 10% of kept items and 100% of critical items (training-distill.md §4.8)
distillation.mix: about 1:1 teacher:gold, subsampled to arm B's training tokens and steps

load_in_4bit.why: Same as arm B, so the only difference is the data.

compute_dtype.why: bf16 where supported, fp16 on a T4; same rule as arm B.

r.why: Same as arm B: equal capacity, so a difference comes from the data.

target_modules.why: Same as arm B; existence in Gemma 4 UNVERIFIED; train_qlora.py excludes vision/audio tower matches and refuses a name with no language-model match.

num_train_epochs.why: Same as arm B; equal steps are enforced by subsampling, not by changing epochs.

max_seq_length.why: Questions are capped at 2,000 characters (example.schema.json); the runner's system prompt is about 1,400 characters and the JSON target is short, so 2048 tokens leaves room; 2048 is also the length behind the models.md §6 VRAM rule. train_qlora.py refuses any record that would be truncated (token counts INFERRED until measured).

training.outputs: Adapter and run_record.json per seed, plus the teacher provenance table (one row per TeacherRecord: teacher id, revision, serving host, terms URL and version, request date, prompt hash, gate result, reviewer).

hardware.assumption: Student: one 16-24 GB GPU, as arm B. Teachers: one 80 GB GPU for gpt-oss-120b and one 40-80 GB GPU for Gemma 4 31B-it (compute class C2), only for the labelling pass.
hardware.vram_estimate: gpt-oss-120b about 65-70 GB with MXFP4; Gemma 4 31B about 20 GB at 4-bit (models.md §3b, INFERRED).
fits: Teachers: no free tier offers an 80 GB GPU, so the teacher pass is a paid rental and is not authorised in Mission 001.

compute.note: Student training is local or free only. The teacher pass needs a rented 80 GB GPU, which is a paid run: it needs the owner's explicit authorisation and the policy sign-off first. No hosted teacher API is permitted by the policy.

cost.basis: Arm B's $0-15 plus the teacher pass: gpt-oss-120b on one H100 80 GB at RunPod Secure $2.89/h (PCIe) to $3.99/h (SXM) and Gemma 4 31B on one A100-80GB at $1.79/h, about 2-6 hours each for 5-20k short structured labels (hours INFERRED), so about $9-35 (2 h x ($2.89 + $1.79) to 6 h x ($3.99 + $1.79)); with arm B's $0-15 the total is about $10-50. The human review of kept items dominates the real cost.
cost.dominant_cost: Human review of teacher labels (at least 10% of kept items, 100% of critical ones) and counsel time for the policy sign-off.
sources: research-notes/cost.md §6: RunPod Secure H100 PCIe $2.89/h, SXM $3.99/h, A100-80GB $1.79/h (VERIFIED, accessed 2026-10-19)
research-notes/training-distill.md §4.2 arm C: 5-20k teacher candidates, 30-60% pass rate (INFERRED)

serving: vLLM with --enable-lora serving the student base at the pinned revision plus the seed adapter, JSON-schema structured outputs.

decoding.why: Same as arm A; differences must come from the adapter only.

evaluation.split_discipline: As arm B. Teachers never see any evaluation prompt.
metrics: subcode_exact (a parent in the subcode field or a parent fallback is wrong)
flags parent_fallback + parent_in_subcode_field (critical; CLE-4): count must be 0
procedure_coarse (via contracts.FINE_TO_COARSE; items with no coarse equivalent are reported as not scorable)
flag procedure_scope_mixed (critical; CLE-3: a visa-scope procedure for a stay question or the reverse): count must be 0
not_status_token_respected and flag code_from_non_code_token ('a 3 month' must not become A-3)
structured-output validity rate (answers with no schema violation)
per adversarial class and per language (ko, en, other) breakdown
teacher gate pass rate and refusal reasons (from the build report)
evaluation.reporting: Mean over 3 seeds with a 95% bootstrap CI; paired comparison against arm B on the same items.

gates.condition: configs/teacher_policy.json legal_signoff is approved by a named reviewer, and every configured teacher is permitted by its entry.
gates.on_fail: No teacher may be served for labelling; train_qlora.py refuses.

gates.condition: As arm B, plus every teacher_generated example has exactly one accepted TeacherRecord whose output equals its expected labels.
Evaluation splits frozen with a committed hash manifest; teachers never received an evaluation prompt.
gates.on_fail: Do not score test or adversarial_holdout.

gates.condition: Arm C starts only after arm B passed G1 and D1 held for arm B.
The runner's flags parent_fallback, parent_in_subcode_field and procedure_scope_mixed occur 0 times on test and adversarial_holdout for every seed, and no metric is worse than arm B beyond its CI.
Arm C beats arm B on adversarial_holdout or non-ko/en items with a 95% bootstrap CI lower bound above 0, at equal training tokens.
Structured-output validity is 1.0 (no schema violation) under constrained decoding.

gates.on_fail: NO-GO for any use beyond offline research.

gates.threshold: p95 well under 7000 ms; exact budget from 12-evaluation-methodology.md

limitations: Teacher agreement is not legal truth; disagreement between the two teachers routes an item to human review, it never votes a label in (training-distill.md §2.1 multi-teacher row).
The teacher generation harness (serving, prompting, ledger writing) is specified here but not built.
Every paid step (teacher rental) needs explicit owner authorisation in addition to the legal sign-off.
